title: Equality Rights Quiz
description: Assesses understanding of equality concepts, protected grounds, and limitation analysis.

questions.question: Equality under the Constitution primarily aims to prevent what?
questions.explanation: Constitutional equality targets unjustified discrimination, not every disparity.

questions.question: Which term best captures a reason the state may not arbitrarily disadvantage a group?
questions.explanation: Protected grounds enumerate characteristics shielded from unfair disadvantage.

questions.question: A law differentiates based on a listed protected ground. Which scrutiny element is LEAST likely relevant?
questions.explanation: Budget surplus is unrelated; limitation analysis focuses on aim, connection, necessity, proportionality.

questions.question: Select ALL components commonly cited in proportionality analysis.
questions.explanation: Legitimate aim, rational connection, and necessity (least restrictive means) are core elements.

questions.question: True or False: Equality always requires identical treatment irrespective of context.
questions.explanation: Substantive equality may justify differential measures to achieve fairness.

questions.question: Scenario: A policy burdens a historically marginalized group. Which analytical factor likely increases scrutiny?
questions.explanation: Historical disadvantage triggers heightened attention to justification quality.

questions.question: Advanced: Which sequence best reflects proportionality steps?
questions.explanation: Standard ordering is legitimate aim, rational connection, necessity, then proportionality balancing (stricto sensu).

questions.question: True or False: Enumerated protected grounds can never be interpreted to include analogous grounds.
questions.explanation: Analogous grounds doctrine may extend protection where similar rationale (e.g., structural exclusion) applies.
